title: Affine quotient of a finite locally free relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be affine schemes over $S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $s,t:R\to U$ be finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Suppose $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $R(H)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(H)$ for every $S$-scheme $H$. Put $C=\{a\in A:s^\sharp(a)=t^\sharp(a)\}$, a subring of $A$. Then $M=\operatorname{Spec}C$ represents the fppf sheafification [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $H\mapsto U(H)/R(H)$. The canonical map $U\to M$ is finite locally free and surjective, $R\cong U\times_MU$ compatibly with the projections, and $M$ has the unique $S$-structure making $U\to M$ a morphism over $S$.

proof.text: Write $\sigma=s^\sharp$, $\tau=t^\sharp$ and $\phi(a\otimes a')=\sigma(a)\tau(a')$. The comparison-preparation lemma gives the absolute groupoid, $qs=qt$, surjectivity of $\phi$ and of $q$, and finite principal-open free covers of $B$ via both maps. If $A=0$, then $B=C=0$ and the empty-scheme case also satisfies the descent and quotient lemmas below; the local hypotheses have no primes to check. In Lean endpoint injectivity is obtained by cancellation against the monomorphism prod.lift s t; Over morphism extensionality identifies the pointwise relation with the preparation lemma’s relation.

source.place: Tags 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence), proof first and second paragraphs; 03BK (lemma-invariants-base-change), (1),(3). Finite free affine descriptions: morphisms.tex Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat).

proof.text: For each prime p of C, the ring C is nonzero and its inclusion into A makes A nonzero. Apply the local-basis reduction to the prepared groupoid and the surjective comparison. Choose its flat local extension C_p → D and apply its universal conclusion to obtain faithful flatness and local basis data. Tensor symmetry transfers finite freeness of A tensor_C D to D tensor_C A. Tensor symmetry, cancellation of base change, and associativity give (A tensor_C D) tensor_D (A tensor_C D) ≅ (A tensor_C A) tensor_C D. The pure-tensor formulas identify the local comparison isomorphism with the base change of phi under this isomorphism. If C has no primes these local conditions are vacuous, so no separate zero-ring argument is necessary.

source.place: Tag 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence), proof fourth and final paragraphs; rank invariance as in Tag 03BI (lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free). Algebraic input: algebra.tex Tag 03C3 (lemma-flat-local-given-residue-field), Tag 03C1 (lemma-semi-local-module-basis-in-submodule); final basis conclusion Tag 03C8 (lemma-basis).

proof.text: Apply flat-local descent using the principal-open free cover from step 1, its surjectivity conclusion for $q$, and the local data from step 2 (vacuous if $A=0$). We obtain that $q$ is finite locally free and surjective, and that $R\to U\times_MU$ is an isomorphism with projections $s,t$. The coordinate comparison is precisely $\phi$, so this is the required compatible isomorphism. Use the source principal-open cover from preparation, with the source homomorphism as the A-algebra structure on B and the target as a C-algebra homomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03BM (proposition-finite-flat-equivalence), proof second paragraph, descent from local flat extensions and finite-presentation descent; algebra.tex Tag 03C4 (lemma-descend-properties-modules), (2), and Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective).

proof.text: Now apply the fppf kernel-pair quotient-descent lemma to $U\to S$, $R\to S$ and this $q$. Its hypotheses hold because the original maps are over $S$, $qs=qt$ by step 1, and step 3 identifies the kernel pair. It gives the unique $S$-structure on $M$ and identifies $h_M$ with the fppf sheafification of $H\mapsto U(H)/R(H)$, completing all clauses. Its universe-lifted Yoneda conclusion implies the ordinary Yoneda conclusion: ULift preserves coequalizers and is fully faithful, so transport the canonical unit through the coequalizer comparison isomorphism and reflect its universal property. ULift preserves and reflects the sheaf condition. These transports are proved private helpers and introduce no additional assumptions or holes.

reviewed_lean.note: Every node clause matches the Lean theorem finiteFlat_affineRelation_quotient. S is an arbitrary scheme; U=Spec A and R=Spec B are over S through Over.mk; s and t are Over-morphisms with IsFiniteLocallyFree (the recorded FiberDegree class: finite, flat, locally of finite presentation). The equivalence-relation hypothesis is Mono (prod.lift s t) plus hrel over all H : Over S. C is RingHom.eqLocus of the Spec.homEquiv coordinate maps (real data), and q is Spec.map of C.subtype (canonical). The conclusions are: q finite locally free and AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective; R isomorphic to pullback q q with fst=s and snd=t; a unique m with q≫m=a; yoneda(Over.mk m) an fppf sheaf; and the canonical η from the Yoneda coequalizer with bijective precomposition into every fppf sheaf (the sheafification universal property). This follows the published EtaleAffineQuotientRepresentable pattern. Nothing is weakened and nothing is added. Edge cases A=0, the identity relation and Spec(k×k) are fine; the universe u is uniform. Every declaration has source and blueprint docstrings, the 13 proof steps are in the docstring, and there is a single sorry. lean.statement is verbatim and the node diff is lean-only. nt_compile --json on the snapshot module compiled clean in 2.0 s, and a probe confirmed the signature, the helper membership equation and the class contents. lean.statement: theorem finiteFlat_affineRelation_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} {A B : CommRingCat.{u}} (a : Spec A ⟶ S) (b : Spec B ⟶ S) (s t : Over.mk b ⟶ Over.mk a) [Mono (prod.lift s t)] [s.left.IsFiniteLocallyFree] [t.left.IsFiniteLocallyFree] (hrel : ∀ H : Over S, Equivalence (fun x y : H ⟶ Over.mk a ↦ ∃ r : H ⟶ Over.mk b, r ≫ s = x ∧ r ≫ t = y)) : (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left).IsFiniteLocallyFree ∧ Surjective (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left) ∧ (∃ e : Spec B ≅ pullback (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left) (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left), e.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = s.left ∧ e.hom ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = t.left) ∧ ∃ m : Spec (CommRingCat.of (affineRelationInvariants s.left t.left)) ⟶ S, ∃ hq : affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left ≫ m = a, (∀ m' : Spec (CommRingCat.of (affineRelationInvariants s.left t.left)) ⟶ S, affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left ≫ m' = a → m' = m) ∧ Presheaf.IsSheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (yoneda.obj (Over.mk m)) ∧ ∃ η : coequalizer (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk m), coequalizer.π (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) ≫ η = yoneda.map (Over.homMk (affineRelationQuotientMap s.left t.left) hq) ∧ ∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun k : yoneda.obj (Over.mk m) ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ k)
lean.note: The two helper definitions specialize RingHom.eqLocus to Spec.homEquiv and take Spec of its subtype inclusion. The quotient presheaf is the Yoneda coequalizer, and its sheafification is expressed by the universal property of the canonical unit, without assuming sheafification of all Type u-valued presheaves on the big site.
